slides.0.subtitle: Riesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc, Vidal and hybrids
slides.1.title: Ontario's grape map
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Varieties in VQA wines
slides.1.highlights.0.content: By volume of VQA wines (April 2025 to March 2026, Wine With Seth): Chardonnay 13%, Riesling 12%, Cabernet Franc 12%, Merlot 11%, Pinot Gris 9%, Vidal Blanc 8%, Sauvignon Blanc 7%, Baco Noir 7%, Cabernet Sauvignon 6%, Pinot Noir 5%, Gamay Noir 3%, Syrah 2%, Gewürztraminer 2%
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Red versus white
slides.1.highlights.1.content: In the same year red made up 47% of VQA wines and white 53%, from 74 varietals. This is a single-year snapshot, useful only for the overall shape
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Cool-climate leaders
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Chardonnay and Riesling lead the whites and Cabernet Franc and Merlot the reds; Pinot Noir and Gamay Noir are also grown but in smaller shares
slides.1.content: Ontario leans on international varieties, with reds and whites in balance.
slides.2.title: Hybrids and Vidal
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Rules for hybrids
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Ontario permits many vinifera varieties and 8 best-of-class hybrids; hybrids must be declared on the label, and a wine with hybrid content may use only the Ontario appellation descriptor and cannot use estate bottled, vineyard designation or Traditional Method; Vidal icewine is the exception (VQA Ontario, Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Vidal and icewine
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Vidal Blanc is the workhorse of icewine: of 468,752 litres of Ontario icewine from April 2025 to March 2026, 388,970 litres were Vidal (Wine With Seth). Its thick skins and cold-hardiness, which let it hang on the vine until frozen, are commonly cited reasons
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Baco Noir and native vines
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Baco Noir is a French hybrid and made up 7% of VQA wines. Of Canada's 13,290 ha of vineyard in 2025, 289 ha were Labrusca and 13,001 ha vinifera or French hybrid (Wine With Seth); in 2001 Niagara data, Concord had the largest planted area at about 10% (AWRI)
slides.2.content: Hybrids are not just extras: Vidal carries icewine.
slides.3.title: British Columbia's grapes
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Reds
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Pinot Noir is the most planted red in BC; Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah follow (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Whites
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The main whites are Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon. For the most planted white, the same site's BC page says Pinot Gris while its Okanagan page lists Chardonnay as the significant variety, so this is not tested
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Warm south, cool north
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The southern Okanagan benches grow Bordeaux varieties (Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc) and Syrah, while the cooler central and northern benches favour Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Riesling and Gewürztraminer (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.content: BC's grape map shifts with the climate from south to north.
